sections.title: In brief
sections.text: March and Knight introduce a theme issue by tracing shape computation from Gips and Stiny’s collaboration through UCLA’s teaching and research program.

sections.title: Editorial purpose
sections.text: What has the research program established, and what theoretical and practical work should follow?

sections.title: Position
sections.text: Shape computation joins geometric rules, transformations and nonshape attributes. Its development includes stylistic analysis, design applications, pedagogy and implementation.

sections.title: How the argument develops
sections.text: The editors combine a historical narrative with a map of the issue’s contributions. This is an interpretive introduction, not a systematic literature review.

sections.title: Examples discussed
sections.text: The editorial points to Prairie-house analysis, grammar implementation, algebraic foundations, Froebel symmetry and Knight’s grammar classifications.

sections.title: Concluding emphasis
sections.text: Implementation remains a central problem. Useful interfaces and understanding what rule systems can predict are presented as practical concerns for designers.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: The account reflects 1999 priorities. A book described as forthcoming or a workshop described as planned should not be read as a current status report.

sections.title: Why read it
sections.text: Use this short article as a map of related research questions before opening the more technical papers.
